brief: A small display stand: three bases meeting at a corner with a raised platform on a spike at that corner.

requirements.requirement: Three bases meeting at a corner
requirements.evidence: Three full hex bases at cells (0,0,0), (1,0,0) and (1,-1,0), mutually adjacent so they share one corner junction. Two joint bolts (jointBolt on (0,0) and (1,-1)) lock them together; the LOOSE_BODY warnings are cleared.

requirements.requirement: Raised platform on a spike at that corner
requirements.evidence: A spike (spike:0#0,0|1,-1|1,0, mount variant) stands at the three-cell junction. setSpikeAccessory with platform-sm returned ok, but the solid spike refused it (TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED), and the platform does not appear as a separate node in get_build, so I could not independently confirm the platform is attached. Treat as likely but unverified.
check_build: ok, meshClash 'clear', no error or loose-body warnings. Only an info note that 12 faces could take caps, which is optional.

finish.summary: Built a corner stand: three full hex bases in a triangle at (0,0), (1,0), (1,-1), locked with two joint bolts, with a mount-type spike at their shared corner and a small platform accessory set on it. Mesh check is clear. The platform attachment returned success but isn't shown as its own node, so it is the one thing I could not fully verify.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

result.note: No place on the build takes this part right now. Change the build so it can (for example add the cells it needs beside or below it), then ask again. Guessing raw ops for a part with no offers rarely works.
